sections.h2: Where is Morrison County and what is the housing market around it like?
sections.html:
Morrison County sits in central Minnesota along the Mississippi River, with Little Falls as its county seat and largest city. The county was carved out of Benton County on February 25, 1856, and covers about 1,153 square miles, of which roughly 1,125 are land. Neighbors are Cass County to the north, Crow Wing to the northeast, Mille Lacs to the east, Benton to the southeast, Stearns to the south and Todd to the west. Camp Ripley Military Reservation takes up a large share of the north-central part of the county.

The Census Bureau's QuickFacts page for Morrison County lists a July 2025 population estimate of 34,620, up from 34,010 in the 2020 census, and 16,659 housing units. Four in five homes are owner-occupied (80.6 percent), the median owner-occupied value for 2020 to 2024 is $248,500, and median gross rent is $788. The median household income is $69,446. Those figures matter at tax time because the assessor values property against recent local sales.

School districts listed for the county include Little Falls, Pierz, Royalton and Staples-Motley, along with Swanville, Upsala, Holdingford and others. A parcel's district shows on its property tax record, so buyers comparing homes in Little Falls and in Pierz are comparing different districts.

sections.h2: Which Morrison County offices handle property taxes?
sections.html:
Three offices cover the work, all in the Morrison County Government Center at 213 1st Avenue SE, Little Falls, MN 56345. The main county line is 320-632-2941, or toll free 1-866-401-1111, and county offices keep hours of Monday to Friday, 8 am to 4:30 pm.

  • Auditor/Treasurer: sends the tax bills, collects the money and holds the payment counter. See the county property tax page.
  • Assessor's Office (Land Services): sets estimated market value and classification, and takes appeal questions at 320-632-0170.
  • Recorder: records deeds and other real estate documents, at 320-632-0146. The recorder's page says the office cannot give legal advice or prepare legal documents, and sends transfer questions to a real estate attorney or an abstract or title company.

For maps and tax statements online, the county points to Beacon. Landshark is its land records system for looking up documents recorded by the recorder's office.

sections.h2: When are Morrison County property taxes due?
sections.html:
Most real property is due in two halves, May 15 and October 15. The county lists separate dates for resorts, manufactured homes and agricultural land, and one rule covers all of them: a due date that lands on a Saturday, Sunday or legal holiday slides to the following business day. Personal property and severed mineral interest taxes are due when real property taxes are.

Morrison County property tax due dates as posted by the county
DateWhat is due
May 15Real property first half, or the whole bill if it is $100 or less
May 31Resorts, first half
August 31Manufactured homes, first half, or the whole bill if $50 or less
October 15Real property, non-agricultural, second half
November 15Agricultural real property second half; manufactured homes second half

In 2026 November 15 falls on a Sunday, so the two November payments slide to Monday, November 16. State law, Minn. Stat. 279.01, sets the same May and October split for bills over $100 and gives agricultural homestead and certain other classes until November 15 for the second half without penalty.

sections.h2: How can you pay Morrison County property tax?
sections.html:
There are six ways, and the county page lists them with the details for each.

  • In person: at the Auditor/Treasurer's Office during office hours, by cash or check payable to Morrison County Auditor/Treasurer.
  • Drop box: on the corner of Broadway (Highway 27) and 2nd Street SE, with payments picked up daily.
  • Mail: to Morrison County Auditor/Treasurer, Government Center, 213 1st Avenue SE, Little Falls, MN 56345. The postmark is the proof of timely mailing and must be on or before the due date.
  • Automatic withdrawal: return the Direct Debit enrollment form at least 30 days before a due date.
  • Online with a card or eCheck: Visa, MasterCard, Discover and American Express are accepted.
  • Phone: 888-272-9829, jurisdiction code 3314. Option 1 is personal property tax, option 2 real estate tax and option 3 mobile home tax.

Card payments carry a convenience fee of 2.59 percent, debit cards 2.59 percent with a $1.10 minimum, and an electronic check costs $2.15.

sections.h2: What penalty applies if a Morrison County tax payment is late?
sections.html:
The penalty starts at 2 percent on homestead property and 4 percent on nonhomestead property once a due date passes with the installment unpaid, and it grows monthly. Under Minn. Stat. 279.01, subdivision 1, a second charge of the same size is added if the installment is still unpaid on the first day of the following month. Each later month through December adds 1 percent. Total penalties stop at 8 percent for homestead and 12 percent for nonhomestead property.

There is a one-time break for mail. The county treasurer must abate the penalty when a payment arrives by mail in an envelope postmarked by the U.S. Postal Service within one business day after the due date, but only for an owner who has not received that abatement before. If the postmark is missing or unreadable, the owner can show proof of mailing by affidavit.

The county board may also let the treasurer abate penalties on a finding that imposing them would be unjust and unreasonable. Ask the Auditor/Treasurer how the county handles such requests.

sections.h2: What can you do if your Morrison County valuation looks too high?
sections.html:
Start with the Assessor's Office, then go to the local board. The county's appeal page explains that you can appeal the current year's estimated market value or classification, which affects taxes payable the following year, and that gathering recent sales of similar properties is the first job.

  1. Collect recent sales of like properties.
  2. Call the Assessor's Office at 320-632-0170 and review your value or classification with a county appraiser.
  3. If it is not settled, make an appointment with your Local Board of Appeal and Equalization, which meets in April.
  4. If you disagree with the local board, appeal to the Special Board of Appeal and Equalization, which meets in June. You must have gone to the local board first, and you need an appointment.
  5. The last step is Minnesota Tax Court.

Meeting dates are printed on your valuation notice and published locally. The 2026 meetings have passed, so the next cycle follows the same April and June pattern. The county adds that the assessor cannot hear an appeal of a prior year's value, which goes only to Tax Court and must be filed by April 30 of the year the taxes are due.

sections.h2: Does a sale of a Morrison County house change the tax picture?
sections.html:
Delinquent tax has to be cleared before a deed can be recorded. Under Minn. Stat. 272.12, the county auditor checks for delinquent taxes when a deed is presented for transfer, and without the auditor's note on the deed the recorder must refuse it. Ask your title company how the current year's taxes will be split between buyer and seller at closing.

A sale also triggers a filing: Minn. Stat. 272.115 requires a certificate of real estate value with the county auditor for sales over $3,000. The assessor then removes the homestead classification for the next assessment year unless the new owner applies for homestead and qualifies. A buyer who has not filed by December 31 is classified nonhomestead for that assessment year.

For sellers who owe back taxes, an inherited house or a property needing repairs, ask the Auditor/Treasurer for the exact balance, including any penalty, before listing.

faqs.q: Who do I call about my Morrison County property taxes?
faqs.a: Call the Auditor/Treasurer through the Government Center main line at 320-632-2941 for payments and balances. The Assessor at 320-632-0170 handles value and classification questions.

faqs.q: When is the second half of property tax due in Morrison County?
faqs.a: October 15 for non-agricultural real property and November 15 for agricultural real property and manufactured homes. A date landing on a Saturday, Sunday or holiday slides ahead to the following business day.

faqs.q: Can I pay Morrison County property tax by credit card?
faqs.a: Yes, online or by phone at 888-272-9829 with jurisdiction code 3314. The county lists a 2.59 percent convenience fee on credit cards.

faqs.q: How do I contest my Morrison County assessment?
faqs.a: Call the Assessor's Office and review your valuation notice with an appraiser, then use the Local Board of Appeal and Equalization in April and the Special Board in June. After that, Minnesota Tax Court is the remaining step.

faqs.q: What is the Morrison County median home value?
faqs.a: The Census Bureau reports a median owner-occupied value of $248,500 for 2020 to 2024. That figure covers the whole county, so a given house in the county may differ a lot from that middle point.
